pl-l4d41c3-d1e115.summary: States that the Church separates those joined within the said degrees of consanguinity.
claims: Marriages within forbidden degrees are separated.

pl-l4d41c3-d1e118.summary: Asks whether, if they were joined in ignorance before the Church and later separated by its judgment on proof of kinship, that union was marriage.

pl-l4d41c3-d1e121.summary: Reports some who think it was not marriage, the persons being unlawful, yet they are excused of crime by ignorance and it is counted as marriage, since they united in good faith and by the Church's hand; so their children are held legitimate.
claims: Good-faith unions count as marriage, and children are legitimate.

pl-l4d41c3-d1e125.summary: Reports others who say it was marriage, though the persons were unlawful, since the canons call such unions marriages where they deal with dissolving them by kin's testimony.
claims: Some hold such unions are true marriages.

pl-l4d41c3.summary: The Church separates those joined within the forbidden degrees. If they married in ignorance before the Church and were later separated by proof of kinship, some say there was no marriage, since they were not lawful persons, but they are excused by ignorance and it counts as marriage, being contracted in good faith through the Church, so their children are legitimate; others say it was marriage, since the canons call such unions marriages.
claims: The Church separates those married within forbidden degrees.
Unions contracted in good faith before the Church have legitimate children.
Whether they were true marriages is disputed.
